malrules.name: Always-Borrow-Left
malrules.description: Students always borrow from the left column in subtraction, even when the top digit is greater than or equal to the bottom digit and borrowing is not needed. This represents an overgeneralization of the borrowing procedure, documented in the BUGGY diagnostic system (Brown & Burton, 1978) and further analyzed in VanLehn's (1990) repair theory research.

malrules.name: Borrow-From-Bottom
malrules.description: When borrowing is needed, students incorrectly decrement the subtrahend (bottom number) instead of the minuend (top number). They add 10 to the top digit correctly but reduce the wrong number's tens digit. This error, documented in Brown & Burton's (1978) BUGGY system, shows a fundamental misunderstanding of which number is being decomposed during regrouping.

malrules.name: Borrow-No-Decrement
malrules.description: When borrowing is required, students correctly add 10 to the current column's digit but forget to decrement the digit in the column they borrowed from. This is one of the most frequently documented subtraction bugs, first catalogued in Brown & Burton's (1978) BUGGY system and extensively analyzed in VanLehn's (1990) Mind Bugs. For example, in 62 - 37, the student makes the ones column 12 - 7 = 5, but leaves the tens as 6 - 3 = 3, giving 35 instead of the correct answer 25.

malrules.name: Decompose-By-Place-Value-Label (Face Value Error)
malrules.description: When interpreting place value decompositions, the student treats the numeric labels as face values to be concatenated rather than as multiplicative values to be added. For example, '2 hundreds 13 tens 1 ones' is written as 2,131 instead of correctly calculating 200 + 130 + 1 = 331. This error reflects what Ross (1989) identified as 'face value' understanding - students interpret digits at their literal face value without understanding their positional significance. The student perceives the decomposition as a labeling task rather than a mathematical composition of values.

malrules.name: Diff-0-N=N (Smaller-From-Larger Variant)
malrules.description: When the minuend digit is 0 and the subtrahend digit is N (where N > 0), the student writes N as the result instead of borrowing. This is a specific manifestation of the 'Smaller-From-Larger' bug documented in Brown & Burton's (1978) BUGGY system, where students subtract the smaller digit from the larger regardless of position. When encountering 0 - N, the student treats this as equivalent to N - 0 = N, avoiding the need to borrow.

malrules.name: No-Column-Limit
malrules.description: When adding multi-digit numbers, students write the entire column sum directly in that column without regrouping, failing to understand the base-10 constraint that each place value position can only hold a single digit (0-9). For example, in 48+17, students compute 8+7=15 and write '15' in the ones column, producing concatenated results like '415' instead of the correct answer 65. This error, documented by the Colorado Department of Education, indicates a fundamental misunderstanding of place value.

malrules.name: Smaller-From-Larger
malrules.description: A systematic procedural bug where the student always subtracts the smaller digit from the larger digit in each column, regardless of position (minuend or subtrahend). This error avoids borrowing by reversing the subtraction when the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit. For example, in 62 - 37, the student computes 7-2=5 in the ones column (instead of borrowing) and 6-3=3 in the tens column, yielding 35 instead of the correct answer 25. This is one of the most extensively documented subtraction bugs in cognitive science research, identified through the BUGGY and DEBUGGY diagnostic systems.

malrules.name: Stops-Borrow-At-Zero
malrules.description: A systematic procedural bug where the student stops the borrowing (regrouping) process entirely when encountering a zero in the column to the left, rather than cascading the borrow further left to find a non-zero digit. This bug is part of a family of zero-related borrowing errors documented in VanLehn's 'Mind Bugs' (1990) and the BUGGY/DEBUGGY diagnostic systems. When students reach an impasse at zero, they may write the absolute difference or simply give up on that column.
